requirements.requirement: node2 runs an HTTP service on TCP 8080 reachable on the private network shared with node1
requirements.summary: Private link 192.168.50.0/24 configured between node1 (vtnet1/opt1=.1) and node2 (enp8s0=.2); simple-http.service confirmed active and listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 with distinctive body 'node2-8080-ok'; curl from node1 over the private IP returned HTTP 200.

requirements.requirement: The service is published on TCP port 80 of node1's management address
requirements.summary: OPNsense config.xml updated with an rdr NAT rule (tcp/80 on vtnet0 -> 192.168.50.2:8080), a matching pass rule for the forwarded flow, and an outbound masquerade rule fixing asymmetric routing; confirmed live via pfctl -s nat showing the rdr entry both before and after node1's reboot, i.e. persisted.

requirements.requirement: node3 can reach the published service on node1:80 and receives the correct content
requirements.summary: curl from node3 to http://10.100.141.10:80/index.html returned HTTP 200 with body 'node2-8080-ok', confirmed at initial verification and again after node3, node2, and node1 reboots.

requirements.requirement: The published port 80 remains refused for every other source address
requirements.summary: A filter reject rule (source != 10.100.141.12) blocks all other traffic to lan-ip:80; verified refused (TCP RST, curl exit 7) from node2 and from node1 itself, both before and after node1's reboot. Direct probes were limited to node1 and node2 (no arbitrary third address was tested), but the rule's structure (single-address allowlist) supports the general claim.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1, node2, node3 with pre/post boot identity, ack, and recovered service/config/data state
requirements.summary: Each node shows a distinct pre-restart boot identity, a background reboot command, a distinct post-restart boot identity, and re-verified functional state after restart (node3: boot_id changed + service reachable; node2: boot_id changed + private IP/systemd unit/firewalld rule persisted + node3 access works; node1: boottime changed, SSH observed down mid-reboot then recovered, NAT/filter config restored from persisted config.xml, and full node3-allow/node2-refuse behavior re-verified). Cross-checked against the fixed after_executor snapshot, which shows different boot-identity values for all three nodes relative to before_prepare/after_prepare.

overall_summary: The task's material requirements are all satisfied with direct evidence: node2's 8080 service is reachable over a newly configured private link, node1 publishes it on management-address port 80 via NAT/filter rules, node3 confirmed reachable with correct content, and other sources (node1, node2) are confirmed refused. The independent full-node restart protocol was also executed and evidenced coherently for all three nodes, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Hygiene is good: the few state-changing troubleshooting steps were either necessary corrections tied to the task or bounded/cleaned up, with no lingering unnecessary residue.
limitations: The 'refused for every other source' claim was tested only from node1 and node2, not from an arbitrary third address outside the topology; conclusion relies partly on the observed firewall rule logic (explicit allow-list for 10.100.141.12) rather than an exhaustive probe.

package-health and failed-services checks are reported as unsupported on node1 (FreeBSD/OPNsense), so hygiene assessment for that node relies on config.xml well-formedness and temp-file diffs rather than a native package-manager consistency check.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor-driven mutations map to necessary steps: private-link IP assignment, systemd service creation, firewalld rich rule, OPNsense NAT/filter rule additions, the anti-lockout http-redirect disable (needed because that built-in rule was unconditionally passing all traffic to port 80 ahead of the new reject rule, and is scoped only to the port-80 redirect since the webgui itself runs on https), and the outbound masquerade fix for an asymmetric-routing bug discovered via diagnostic curls. A first 'configctl interface reload' attempt (cmd-771aadbc84254851) failed ('Action not allowed or missing') but caused no residue and was immediately corrected by the working 'configctl interface reconfigure opt1' (cmd-5c35369dcfed4e88). The executor cleaned up its scratch files, including the config.xml backup, via cmd-b5e694070ce3480b; only expected reboot.log residue and normal systemd-private temp dirs remain per the after_executor snapshot. No unnecessary, unrelated, or unreverted mutations were found in the timeline; no failed or conflicting services and no package-state damage are evident in the before/after comparisons.
